Near the Hudson River, there was a small, quiet valley where everything seemed to move in a dream. <break time="0.8s" /> People called it Sleepy Hollow, and they said that a drowsy, dreamy spirit hung over the whole land. <break time="0.8s" /> The people there loved strange stories, and they often saw odd sights and heard music in the air. <break time="0.8s" /> The most famous ghost of the valley was a rider on horseback who had no head at all. <break time="0.8s" /> Some said he was the ghost of a soldier who had lost his head to a cannonball in the war. <break time="0.8s" /> Every night, people said, he rode out to the old battlefield, searching for his lost head. <break time="0.8s" /> His body was said to lie in the churchyard, so he always hurried back there before daybreak. <break time="0.8s" /> In this valley lived a schoolteacher named Ichabod Crane, who had come from Connecticut to teach the local children. <break time="0.8s" /> He was tall and very thin, with long arms, huge ears, and a long nose like a birds beak. <break time="0.8s" /> Seeing him walk across a hill on a windy day, you might take him for a scarecrow.

허드슨강 근처에. <break time="0.8s" /> 작고 조용한 골짜기가 하나 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳에서는 모든 것이 움직이는 듯했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 꿈속에서처럼. <break time="0.8s" /> 사람들은 그곳을 슬리피 할로라고 불렀다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그들은 말했다 졸리고 꿈결 같은 기운이. <break time="0.8s" /> 온 땅을 덮고 있다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그곳 사람들은. <break time="0.8s" /> 이상한 이야기를 좋아했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그들은 자주 기이한 광경을 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 허공에서 음악 소리를 들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 골짜기에서 가장 유명한 유령은. <break time="0.8s" /> 말을 탄 기수였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 머리가 아예 없는. <break time="0.8s" /> 어떤 사람들은 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그가 한 병사의 유령이라고. <break time="0.8s" /> 머리를 잃은. <break time="0.8s" /> 전쟁 때 대포알에 맞아서. <break time="0.8s" /> 매일 밤. <break time="0.8s" /> 사람들 말로는. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 옛 싸움터로 말을 타고 나갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 잃어버린 머리를 찾으면서. <break time="0.8s" /> 그의 몸은 누워 있다고 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 교회 묘지에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 그는 늘 그곳으로 서둘러 돌아갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 날이 밝기 전에. <break time="0.8s" /> 이 골짜기에 살았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 이카보드 크레인이라는 학교 선생이. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 코네티컷에서 왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 지역 아이들을 가르치려고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 키가 크고 무척 말랐다. <break time="0.8s" /> 긴 팔과 큰 귀를 가졌고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 긴 코를 가졌다. <break time="0.8s" /> 새의 부리 같은. <break time="0.8s" /> 그가 언덕을 걸어가는 것을 보면. <break time="0.8s" /> 바람 부는 날에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그를 허수아비로 착각할지도 모른다.

Ichabod lived. <break time="0.8s" /> With the families of his students. <break time="0.8s" /> Staying a week at each house. <break time="0.8s" /> In turn. <break time="0.8s" /> He helped with the farm work. <break time="0.8s" /> Taught singing on Sundays. <break time="0.8s" /> And was popular. <break time="0.8s" /> With the women of the valley. <break time="0.8s" /> He loved ghost stories. <break time="0.8s" /> And on winter evenings. <break time="0.8s" /> He listened to the old wives tales. <break time="0.8s" /> Until he trembled. <break time="0.8s" /> Walking home in the dark afterward. <break time="0.8s" /> He jumped at every shadow. <break time="0.8s" /> And sang loudly. <break time="0.8s" /> To keep up his courage. <break time="0.8s" /> Among his singing students. <break time="0.8s" /> Was Katrina Van Tassel. <break time="0.8s" /> The only daughter. <break time="0.8s" /> Of a very rich Dutch farmer. <break time="0.8s" /> She was eighteen. <break time="0.8s" /> With rosy cheeks. <break time="0.8s" /> And she was famous. <break time="0.8s" /> For both her beauty and her fathers money. <break time="0.8s" /> When Ichabod saw the fat pigs, turkeys. <break time="0.8s" /> And wide fields. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the Van Tassel farm. <break time="0.8s" /> His eyes shone. <break time="0.8s" /> If I married Katrina. <break time="0.8s" /> All of this would be mine. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Picturing every pig. <break time="0.8s" /> As a roast dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> But Ichabod had a rival. <break time="0.8s" /> Brom Bones. <break time="0.8s" /> The strongest young man in the valley. <break time="0.8s" /> And its best horseman. <break time="0.8s" /> Brom loved pranks. <break time="0.8s" /> And whenever his horse was tied. <break time="0.8s" /> At the Van Tassels fence. <break time="0.8s" /> Other young men stayed away.

Ichabod lived with the families of his students, staying a week at each house in turn. <break time="0.8s" /> He helped with the farm work, taught singing on Sundays, and was popular with the women of the valley. <break time="0.8s" /> He loved ghost stories, and on winter evenings he listened to the old wives tales until he trembled. <break time="0.8s" /> Walking home in the dark afterward, he jumped at every shadow and sang loudly to keep up his courage. <break time="0.8s" /> Among his singing students was Katrina Van Tassel, the only daughter of a very rich Dutch farmer. <break time="0.8s" /> She was eighteen, with rosy cheeks, and she was famous for both her beauty and her fathers money. <break time="0.8s" /> When Ichabod saw the fat pigs, turkeys, and wide fields of the Van Tassel farm, his eyes shone. <break time="0.8s" /> If I married Katrina, all of this would be mine, he thought, picturing every pig as a roast dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> But Ichabod had a rival, Brom Bones, the strongest young man in the valley and its best horseman. <break time="0.8s" /> Brom loved pranks, and whenever his horse was tied at the Van Tassels fence, other young men stayed away.

Brom wanted to fight Ichabod. <break time="0.8s" /> But Ichabod knew that if he fought Brom. <break time="0.8s" /> He would surely lose. <break time="0.8s" /> So Brom played tricks on him instead. <break time="0.8s" /> Stopping up his chimney. <break time="0.8s" /> And filling the schoolhouse with smoke. <break time="0.8s" /> He even trained a dog. <break time="0.8s" /> To whine in a silly way. <break time="0.8s" /> As if it were a rival singing teacher. <break time="0.8s" /> One autumn afternoon. <break time="0.8s" /> A messenger arrived at the school. <break time="0.8s" /> With an invitation to a party. <break time="0.8s" /> At the Van Tassels. <break time="0.8s" /> Ichabod let the children go home. <break time="0.8s" /> An hour early. <break time="0.8s" /> And spent extra time. <break time="0.8s" /> Brushing his only black suit. <break time="0.8s" /> He borrowed an old plow horse. <break time="0.8s" /> Named Gunpowder. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was thin, half blind. <break time="0.8s" /> And still full of mischief. <break time="0.8s" /> At the farm. <break time="0.8s" /> The tables were covered. <break time="0.8s" /> With cakes, pies, and meats. <break time="0.8s" /> And Ichabod ate until he was full. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he danced with Katrina. <break time="0.8s" /> Smiling happily. <break time="0.8s" /> While Brom sat alone in a corner. <break time="0.8s" /> Sick with jealousy. <break time="0.8s" /> Later the guests told ghost stories. <break time="0.8s" /> And many of them were about the Headless Horseman. <break time="0.8s" /> Brom said. <break time="0.8s" /> He had raced the Horseman. <break time="0.8s" /> To the church bridge. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the ghost vanished. <break time="0.8s" /> In a flash of fire.
